extracted.intended_audience: prospective offerors/applicants responding to the ONR BAA (contractors, universities, non-profits, and other organizations seeking ONR contracts or other transaction agreements)
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and evaluation-related criteria for preparing and submitting full proposals in response to the Office of Naval Research Broad Agency Announcement (contracts and other transaction agreements), including certifications, reporting, format, content, and conflict-of-interest mitigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of designated integrity and performance systems (SAM)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant, at its option, may review information in the designated integrity and performance systems accessible through SAM and comment on any information about itself that a Federal awarding agency previously entered and is currently in the designated integrity and performance system accessible through SAM; The Federal awarding agency will consider any comments by the applicant, in addition to the other information in the designated integrity and performance system, in making a judgment about the applicant’s integrity, business ethics, and record of performance under Federal awards when completing the review of risk posed by applicants as described in 2 CFR 200.206.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may and should review their SAM entries and provide comments; agencies will consider applicant comments alongside other information when assessing responsibility and risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Funding Accountability and Transparency Act (FFATA) reporting capability
rubrics_metrics.description: Entities applying for financial assistance must provide information in their proposal that describes the necessary processes and systems in place to comply with the reporting requirements identified in 2 CFR Part 170 (reporting on subawards and executive total compensation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must describe processes/systems (and meet reporting requirements unless an exception/exemption applies). Refer to 2 CFR Part 170 and Appendix A for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial Assistance Certifications (attestations and disclosures)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal Assistance Certifications Report attests the entity will abide by laws and supplemental requirements; applicants are required to submit documentation including SF-LLL (Disclosure of Lobby Activities) if applicable, and disclosure of any unpaid delinquent tax liability or felony conviction under any Federal law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission of required certifications/attestations is mandatory as applicable; false statements may trigger penalties. Include SF-LLL when required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification regarding restrictions on lobbying
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants > $100,000 require a certification of compliance with lobbying restrictions (SF424 Block 17); cooperative agreements seeking federal assistance funds exceeding $10,000 are likewise covered. The certification states that no Federal appropriated funds have been/will be paid to influence Federal officials in connection with awarding or modifying Federal contracts/grants/loans/cooperative agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If non-Federal funds are paid for lobbying activity, submit SF-LLL. Include the certification language in award documents for all subawards at all tiers. Failure to file required certification subjects person to civil penalties ($10,000–$100,000 per failure).

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification re: internal confidentiality agreements (GIC 19-02)
rubrics_metrics.description: By signing SF424 (R&R) Block 17, the applicant certifies it does not require employees/contractors/subrecipients seeking to report fraud, waste, or abuse to sign or comply with internal confidentiality agreements that prohibit lawful reporting to designated Federal investigative or law enforcement representatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checking 'I Agree' indicates understanding that false statements may result in criminal/civil/administrative penalties (18 U.S.C. §1001).

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification regarding disclosure of funding sources (NDAA Sec. 223(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: By checking 'I Agree' on SF424 (R&R) Block 17, the proposing entity certifies compliance with Section 223(a) of the William M. (Mac) Thornberry NDAA FY2021: (a) PI and key personnel certify current and pending support is current, accurate and complete; (b) agree to update such disclosure at the agency's request prior to award and during the award term as the agency determines appropriate; (c) PI and key personnel have been made aware of the requirements under Section 223(a)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: False statements may subject individuals to penalties (18 U.S.C. §1001). Update disclosures promptly if requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of Interest — general disclosure requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must comply with 2 CFR 200.318(c) Codes of Conduct to prevent real or apparent conflicts of interest in procurement supported by federal funds. You and your organization must disclose any potential or actual scientific or nonscientific conflict(s) of interest to ONR, including for any identified subrecipient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ONR may request additional information or a mitigation plan at its discretion; nondisclosure or misrepresentation may lead to disqualification, termination, or other remedial actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific conflict of interest guidance (collaborations and current/pending support)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific collaborations that result from close pre-submission collaboration should be considered when identifying potential conflicts. Offerors must include in current and pending support all collaborators even if they did not formally provide support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List collaborators in current/pending support to ensure proper conflict assessment; ONR may request further details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational Conflict of Interest (OCI) disclosure statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Offerors must state whether they are aware of any actual or potential OCI per FAR 2.101 and FAR Subpart 9.5 for themselves and proposed subcontractors/partners/consultants/affiliates. Offerors not providing support services to ONR should include a specific 'NO actual or potential OCI exists' certification statement. Offerors who do provide support or are aware of circumstances that may create an OCI must submit specified information (entity supported, contract number, description of OCI, mitigation plan, concluding certification).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nondisclosure or misrepresentation of an OCI can disqualify an offeror or lead to contract termination/default and other remedies (see 18 U.S.C. §1001 and 31 U.S.C. §3802(a)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: OCI Mitigation Plan minimum contents
rubrics_metrics.description: A Mitigation Plan shall, at minimum: (i) provide organizational charts showing structure as it relates to performance and all contracts/agreements relevant to the OCI; (ii) demonstrate how elements creating the OCI will be isolated from resources performing the work; (iii) show whether performing elements will be geographically/physically separated; (iv) describe personnel reassignment processes and restrictions; (v) describe controls (including nondisclosure agreements) over future employment of departing employees as it relates to the OCI; (vi) describe OCI training offered/required (timing, frequency, length, content); (vii) provide evidence of facts/circumstances that mitigate/address OCI concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Contracting Officer will review mitigation plans and may request more information. If an OCI cannot be mitigated, the offeror will be ineligible for award. If accepted, the Mitigation Plan becomes part of the contract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review for basic research projects
rubrics_metrics.description: For proposals funded as basic research, ONR may utilize peer reviewers from academia, industry, and government to assist in periodic appraisal of performance under awards (per ONR Instruction 3966.1A). Peer reviewers who are not U.S. Government employees must sign nondisclosure agreements before receiving full/partial copies of proposals and reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Periodic peer reviews may affect continued funding. Offerors may include PI travel costs to attend peer review. Peer reviews may consider information from project/program review meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on certain telecommunications and video surveillance equipment/services (Section 889)
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with 2 CFR 200.216 and related law, recipients and subrecipients are prohibited from obligating or expending federal funds to procure, extend, renew, or enter into contracts to procure equipment, services, or systems that use covered telecommunications equipment or services as a substantial/essential component or critical technology. Covered equipment includes telecom equipment produced by Huawei or ZTE and certain video surveillance equipment by Hytera, Hikvision, or Dahua, and equipment/services produced by entities reasonably believed to be owned/controlled by a covered foreign country (defined as the People's Republic of China).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies shall prioritize available funding/technical support to assist affected entities to transition from covered equipment as necessary. See Public Law 115-232, section 889 for additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of post-award reporting for Recipient Integrity and Performance Matters
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Federal share of any Federal award may include more than $500,000 over the period of performance, the Award Term and Condition for Recipient Integrity and Performance Matters (2 CFR Part 200 Appendix XII) is applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applicable, the detailed post-award reporting requirements described in Appendix XII must be followed; see ONR addendum link for post award reporting requirements and terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-award reporting of matters related to recipient integrity and performance (SAM reporting thresholds and content)
rubrics_metrics.description: If your total currently active Federal grants, cooperative agreements, and procurement contracts exceed $10,000,000 at any time during the award period, you must maintain current information in SAM about civil, criminal, or administrative proceedings in connection with Federal awards reaching final disposition during the most recent five-year period and meeting specific thresholds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reportable proceedings include: (i) criminal convictions; (ii) civil proceedings with fault and monetary payment of $5,000 or more; (iii) administrative proceedings with fault and payment of $5,000+ or reimbursement/restitution/damages > $100,000; (iv) other proceedings that could have led to these outcomes, including consent/compromise with acknowledgment of fault, provided reporting does not conflict with law. Enter required information in SAM Entity Management; do not resubmit if already reported under procurement awards. Reporting frequency: maintain five-year currency and, if cumulative federal awards exceed $10M, disclose semiannually any criminal/civil/administrative proceedings. Definitions for terms like administrative proceeding, conviction, and total value of active awards are provided in the award term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal package required documents (full proposal content)
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete proposal package includes: (1) Cover page (pdf), (2) Proposal Checklist (pdf), (3) Technical Proposal Template (Word), (4) Cost Proposal Template (Excel) for the prime and all proposed subcontractors, (5) DCAA Pre-award Survey of Prospective Contractor Accounting System Checklist (if contractor lacks approved accounting system) (pdf), (6) Statement of Work (SOW) (Word), (7) ONR Contract Specific Representations and Certifications (pdf).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Items 1–6 are located on the ONR site and include embedded instructions. Attachments can be incorporated in the Proposal Checklist. The Cover Page is required for FedConnect to accept a proposal package. Include the Program Office’s correct email address to ensure delivery to the Program Officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal formatting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Format requirements for attachments: paper size 8.5 x 11-inch; margins 1 inch; spacing single or double-spaced; font Times New Roman, 12 point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow these formatting rules for all documents; specific templates have embedded instructions to assist completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual property/technical data/software rights identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Offerors must submit a separate list of all technical data or computer software to be furnished to the Government with other than unlimited rights in the proposal checklist. The Government will assume unlimited rights if offerors fail to identify any intellectual property restrictions. Include all proprietary claims to results, prototypes, and/or deliverables. If no restrictions are intended, state 'NONE'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identification of IP restrictions is required to preserve rights claims; omission will be treated as unlimited rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost proposal and spreadsheet content/format requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost Proposal Template (Excel) is required for prime and all proposed subcontractors. For proposed subcontracts or inter-organizational transfers over $250K, offerors must provide a separate fully completed Cost Proposal Spreadsheet in support of the proposed costs. The Cost Proposal Spreadsheet must be submitted in Microsoft Excel format; the Statement of Work Template must be Word. All other documents except Cost Proposal Spreadsheet and SOW must be submitted in secure, pdf-compatible format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secure pdf-compatible format should prevent unauthorized editing; do not require a password to open. If subcontract info is proprietary, it may be submitted via e-mail to the Program Officer with identification of the proposal and subcontractor. Any options identified but not fully priced will not be included in a resulting award; options must be separately priced with separate spreadsheets for base and each option. Provide a breakdown of cost for each SOW task; sums of task worksheets must equal total cost summary. Excel spreadsheets must be in 'useable condition'—visibly include inputs, formulas, calculations; do not provide 'value only' spreadsheets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixed fees and contract type fee guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Fixed Fees on ONR Contracts: Government objective set per DFARS 215.404-71. Table provides ranges and normal values for Contract Risk Factor and Assigned Value by Contract Type. Technology Incentive (TI) is rarely utilized; typical fee range on ONR-awarded contracts is 5% to 7.5%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign weight percentages to technical and management/cost control elements so totals equal 100%. TI requires strong justification and is subject to negotiation; use DFARS guidance for assigning weights and normal values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Government-Furnished Equipment/Facilities (GFE/GFM/GFI) disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Government research facilities and operational military units are available as potential government-furnished equipment/facilities and should be considered. Offerors should indicate in the Proposal Checklist which facilities/test sites are critical for project success and specify whether they will require GFE, GFM, and GFI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These facilities/resources are high value and in demand; use will be negotiated as programs unfold. Clearly state GFE/GFM/GFI needs in Proposal Checklist Section II Blocks 9a/9b.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ammunition & explosives (A&E) safety and security requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If ammunitions and/or explosives are to be utilized, the Offeror must comply with DoD manual 4145.26-M (DoD Contractor's Safety Manual for Ammunition and Explosives) and related DFARS clauses; a preaward safety survey (SF 1403) is required. If Government provides A&E containing nitrocellulose-based propellants or nitrate ester-based materials, NMCARS 5252.223-9000 applies. For sensitive (Security Risk Category I–IV) AA&E, a preaward security survey is required and the Government may require perimeter fencing. Offerors must provide written AA&E accountability procedures if required, and should include them with the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference specific DFARS/NMCARS and DoD manual requirements; include required safety/security documentation and be prepared for preaward surveys.

rubrics_metrics.name: System for Award Management (SAM) registration & maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: FAR 52.204-7 (SAM) and FAR 52.204-13 (SAM Maintenance) are incorporated into the BAA and will be incorporated into all awards. Organizations must register with SAM (have a UEI) to apply online. The first person in an organization to register in FedConnect will need the SAM MPIN.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Register early at https://sam.gov. Maintain current information in SAM as required by incorporated clauses and post-award reporting terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: FedConnect submission portal and assistance rules
rubrics_metrics.description: ONR is using FedConnect to accept full proposals for contracts and OT agreements. FedConnect will not accept a proposal package unless the Cover Page is included. Do not use the FedConnect Message Center to submit questions or proposals. FedConnect support contact info and a 'Ready Set Go' guide are provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow FedConnect instructions (guide pages 25–33) for submission steps. If assistance is needed, contact fcsupport@unisonglobal.com or the Program Office contacts in Section G. Do not use the FedConnect Message Center for questions or proposal submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility determination and FAR 9.104-1 standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracts shall be awarded to responsible prospective contractors only per FAR 9.104-1. Applicants are requested to provide information with proposal submission to assist the Contracting Officer’s evaluation of responsibility. The Responsibility/Qualification section of SAM.gov (FAPIIS) is used in making judgments about an entity's integrity, business ethics, and record of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offerors may comment on FAPIIS entries about their entity. Provide requested information to assist the Contracting Officer; FAPIIS information will influence responsibility determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation of applicable FAR/DFARS/NMCARS clauses
rubrics_metrics.description: ONR may include relevant FAR, DFARS, or NMCARS clauses in final awards based on award dollar value. The solicitation lists example provisions/clauses that may be applicable (e.g., FAR 52.204-7, 52.215-20, 52.216-1, 52.217-4, 52.222-50, DFARS/NMCARS clauses, and others).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offerors should be familiar with referenced clauses and prepared to accept applicable clauses in resulting awards; consult acquisition.gov for clause text.
